quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular, white, and have black lettering. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow them.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line or sign first. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: To be effective, eye or face shield protection must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Able to fasten securely.
Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
Free of scratches.
Able to allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, fasten securely, allow clear side views, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if you need them.

questions.question: To lessen your chances of being in a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch about five feet ahead of your motorcycle while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid a sudden hazard.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab at the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab at the rear brake.
Press down on the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Allow a clear view to both sides.
Prevent air from passing through it.
Be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting underneath it.
Should not fasten too tightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air flow through, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Passing and being passed when riding a motorcycle is not much different than when driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than that of a car.
A motorcycle's visibility is not as important as that of a car.
Passing should be done on the shoulder instead of on the main roadway.
It is critical to make eye contact with the other driver when riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than that of a car.
questions.explanation: Visibility is more important when riding a motorcycle than when driving a car. A motorcycle is smaller and easier to miss. Other drivers may not see you even when looking, or you may disappear into their blind spot.

questions.question: Riders who do not wear helmets while riding are ________ to die in a crash than riders who do wear helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, no matter how fast they are going.

questions.question: When making an ordinary stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for special situations.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for special situations.
Sharply squeeze the front brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you practice this habit, you will be able to use both brakes quickly when you need to stop fast.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Signal your intentions by using your turn signals and brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.
Hope other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce your crash risk, be visible to other drivers, signal your intentions, and keep space around you. Look for hazards and be ready to react to anything.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the bike straight. Brake slowly on the good tire only. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Only take a few minutes.
Take more than an hour.
Be complicated to perform.
Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only take a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Do a careful inspection of your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic there.
A dangerous spot for riders.
Hard to understand.
Safer than the open road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A dangerous spot for riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because they have the most conflicts between riders and other drivers.

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, what does it mean?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals to show turns or stops when they don't have turn signals. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:

options.text: Far from home.
On short trips.
On long rides.
Several hours into the ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting out.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, how will the steering feel?

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
The same as normal.
Too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Why should riders in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see.
Riders don't have enough space to avoid hazards.
It is too hard for left-side riders to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders don't have enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should not ride side by side. Neither rider will have enough room to move and avoid hazards.

questions.question: When can motorcycles use High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes?

options.text: Only when it is raining.
Only on weekends.
Only when carrying a passenger.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: At any time.
questions.explanation: In Washington State, motorcycles can use HOV lanes at any time unless a sign says otherwise. HOV lanes have diamond markings on the road and signs.

questions.question: What should you do to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do?

options.text: Do not need space cushions.
Increase their space cushions.
Reduce their space cushions by half.
Keep adequate space cushions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep adequate space cushions.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, keep an adequate space cushion around each rider, even while riding close together.

questions.question: Why should you use both brakes every time you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake causes uneven brake wear.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
It is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes in normal stops builds the habit of always using both. This habit helps in emergencies when using both brakes is critical.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your whole face.
It is less effective than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When braking on surfaces with poor traction, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brakes harder than usual.
Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
Do not use the rear brake.
Do not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
questions.explanation: On surfaces with poor traction, apply the brakes more gently than usual.
